title: Earth & Space Science (6th Grade)
description: Earth & Space Science (6th Grade) practice - 100 questions

questions.question: What are tectonic plates?
questions.correctAnswer: Large pieces of Earth's crust and upper mantle that move slowly
questions.explanation: Earth's lithosphere is broken into tectonic plates that drift on the mantle.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Earth's surface is a jigsaw of moving plates.

questions.question: What is the geosphere?
questions.correctAnswer: The solid part of Earth, including rock and soil
questions.explanation: The geosphere is the solid Earth under your feet: the crust, mantle, and core, plus all the rocks and soil.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The geosphere is Earth's solid ground.

questions.question: What instrument measures air pressure?
questions.correctAnswer: A barometer
questions.explanation: A barometer measures air pressure, which helps predict weather changes.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Falling pressure often means a storm is coming.

questions.question: What is the epicenter of an earthquake?
questions.correctAnswer: The point on Earth's surface above where the quake started
distractors: The deepest part of the fault
The place with the most damage only
questions.explanation: The epicenter is directly above the focus, where the rocks first broke.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The epicenter is the spot on the surface above the break.

questions.question: What is a volcano?
questions.correctAnswer: An opening where lava, ash, and gases erupt
distractors: A mountain made only of ice
A hole made by a meteor
questions.explanation: A volcano is an opening in Earth's crust where molten rock and gases escape.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Volcanoes let Earth's hot insides out.

questions.question: How many planets are in our solar system?
questions.explanation: There are 8 planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: My Very Excellent Mother Just Served Us Nachos.

questions.question: Which type of rock is sandstone?
questions.correctAnswer: Sedimentary
questions.explanation: Sandstone forms from sand grains pressed and cemented together.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sandstone is glued-together sand.

questions.question: What is climate?
questions.correctAnswer: The average weather of a place over a long time
questions.explanation: Climate looks at decades of weather records, so one rainy day does not change a desert's climate.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Climate is what you expect; weather is what you get.

questions.question: What is an equinox?
questions.correctAnswer: A day when day and night are nearly equal
distractors: The longest day of the year
The shortest day of the year
questions.explanation: At an equinox, the Sun is directly over the equator and day and night are about equal.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Equinox means equal night.

questions.question: What is the asthenosphere?
questions.correctAnswer: The soft, slowly flowing part of the upper mantle
questions.explanation: The asthenosphere is hot, soft mantle rock that tectonic plates slide on.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Plates glide on the soft asthenosphere.

questions.question: What is weather?
questions.correctAnswer: The state of the atmosphere at a certain place and time
questions.explanation: Weather describes short-term conditions like temperature, rain, and wind right now.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Weather is what is happening outside today.

questions.question: What is a galaxy?
questions.correctAnswer: A huge system of stars, gas, and dust held by gravity
questions.explanation: Galaxies contain billions of stars; ours is the Milky Way.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A galaxy is a city of stars.

questions.question: What is the hydrosphere?
questions.correctAnswer: All the water on Earth
questions.explanation: The hydrosphere includes oceans, lakes, rivers, ice, groundwater, and water vapor.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The hydrosphere is Earth's water.

questions.question: What is a cold front?
questions.correctAnswer: Cold air pushing under warm air
distractors: Warm air rising over cold air
questions.explanation: A cold front brings colder air that slides under warm air, often causing storms.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cold fronts shove warm air up fast.

questions.question: What gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.correctAnswer: Nitrogen
questions.explanation: About 78% of the air is nitrogen, and about 21% is oxygen.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Most of the air you breathe is nitrogen.

questions.question: What do we call frozen water falling from clouds?
questions.correctAnswer: Snow
questions.explanation: Snow is precipitation made of ice crystals.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Snowflakes are frozen precipitation.

questions.question: What is the outermost layer of Earth called?
questions.correctAnswer: The crust
questions.explanation: The crust is the thin, solid outer layer of Earth that we live on.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The crust is Earth's crunchy outer shell.

questions.question: What is the atmosphere?
questions.correctAnswer: The layer of gases around Earth
distractors: The layer of rock on Earth
questions.explanation: The atmosphere's gases - mostly nitrogen and oxygen - let us breathe, carry weather, and shield Earth from space.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The atmosphere is the air around Earth.

questions.question: What is a mineral?
questions.correctAnswer: A natural solid with a definite chemical makeup
questions.explanation: Minerals are natural, solid substances with a set chemical composition and crystal structure.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Minerals are nature's building blocks.

questions.question: What is a rock?
questions.correctAnswer: A solid made of one or more minerals
questions.explanation: Most rocks are a mix: granite, for example, is made of quartz, feldspar, and mica minerals stuck together.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Rocks are built from minerals.

questions.question: What is the center of Earth called?
questions.correctAnswer: The inner core
questions.explanation: The inner core is the solid, hottest part at the very center of Earth.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The inner core is a solid ball of hot metal.

questions.question: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.correctAnswer: The Sun
questions.explanation: The Sun is the star at the center of our solar system, closest to Earth.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Our Sun is a star, just a close one.

questions.question: What is the greenhouse effect?
questions.correctAnswer: Gases trapping heat in the atmosphere
questions.explanation: Greenhouse gases absorb heat and keep Earth warm enough for life.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Greenhouse gases act like a blanket for Earth.

questions.question: What is a front in weather?
questions.correctAnswer: The boundary where two air masses meet
questions.explanation: Fronts are boundaries between warm and cold air masses, often bringing changing weather.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fronts are where air masses collide.

questions.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.correctAnswer: Mars
questions.explanation: Mars looks red because of rusty iron dust on its surface.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mars is red from rusty dust.

questions.question: Why do we have leap years?
questions.correctAnswer: Earth's orbit takes about 365.25 days
questions.explanation: An extra day every four years makes up for the extra quarter day in each orbit.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Leap day catches up the quarter days.

questions.question: What is the mantle?
questions.correctAnswer: The thick layer of hot rock between the crust and the core
distractors: The thin outer shell of Earth
The layer of air around Earth
questions.explanation: The mantle is the thickest layer, made of hot rock that can flow very slowly.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The mantle is the thick, hot middle layer.

questions.question: What causes wind?
questions.correctAnswer: Differences in air pressure
questions.explanation: Air moves from high-pressure areas to low-pressure areas, creating wind.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Wind is air moving from high to low pressure.

questions.question: What is the difference between a transform boundary and a convergent boundary?
questions.correctAnswer: Transform plates slide past each other; convergent plates collide
distractors: Transform plates collide; convergent plates slide
questions.explanation: Transform boundaries cause earthquakes as plates grind past - the San Andreas Fault is a famous one - while convergent boundaries can build mountains or cause subduction.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Slide past versus crash together.

questions.question: What is the water cycle?
questions.correctAnswer: The movement of water between Earth and the atmosphere
questions.explanation: The water cycle is the continuous movement of water through evaporation, condensation, and precipitation.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Water travels in a big circle: up, over, and down.

questions.question: What is weathering?
questions.correctAnswer: The breaking down of rock into smaller pieces
distractors: The movement of rock by water
questions.explanation: Weathering breaks rocks apart in place through water, wind, ice, or living things.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Weathering breaks rocks where they sit.

questions.question: How long does it take the Moon to orbit Earth?
questions.correctAnswer: About 27 days
questions.explanation: The Moon takes about 27.3 days to complete one orbit around Earth.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Moon's month is about 27 days.

questions.question: What gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
questions.correctAnswer: Carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen during photosynthesis.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Plants breathe in carbon dioxide.

questions.question: What is subduction?
questions.correctAnswer: One tectonic plate sinking below another
questions.explanation: At some convergent boundaries, a dense oceanic plate sinks under another plate.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Subduction is one plate diving under another.

questions.question: What are the layers of the atmosphere from lowest to highest?
questions.correctAnswer: Troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere
questions.explanation: Weather happens in the troposphere, the lowest layer, with the stratosphere above it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Weather lives in the troposphere at the bottom.

questions.question: What is the difference between a meteoroid, a meteor, and a meteorite?
questions.correctAnswer: A meteoroid is in space, a meteor burns in the sky, and a meteorite lands on Earth
distractors: They are three names for the same thing
A meteor is in space and a meteoroid lands
A meteorite burns in the sky
questions.explanation: A meteoroid in space becomes a meteor (shooting star) in the atmosphere, and a meteorite if it hits the ground.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Space, sky, ground: meteoroid, meteor, meteorite.

questions.question: What is a light-year?
questions.correctAnswer: The distance light travels in one year
distractors: The time light takes to reach Earth
questions.explanation: A light-year is a unit of distance, about 9.5 trillion kilometers.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A light-year measures distance, not time.

questions.question: What is groundwater?
questions.correctAnswer: Water stored in soil and rock below the surface
questions.explanation: Groundwater fills cracks and spaces in underground rock and soil.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Groundwater hides below your feet.

questions.question: What is a warm front?
questions.correctAnswer: Warm air sliding over cold air
distractors: Cold air pushing under warm air
A front that only brings snow
questions.explanation: A warm front brings warmer air that rises gently over cold air, often causing steady rain.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Warm fronts slide in gently.

questions.question: What does a seismograph measure?
questions.correctAnswer: The motion of the ground during an earthquake
questions.explanation: A seismograph records ground motion from seismic waves.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Seismographs draw the shaking of earthquakes.

questions.question: Which planet has the most visible rings?
questions.correctAnswer: Saturn
questions.explanation: Saturn's rings are made of ice and rock and are the most prominent in the solar system.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Saturn wears the brightest rings.

questions.question: What is the Moon?
questions.correctAnswer: A natural satellite of Earth
questions.explanation: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite, orbiting our planet.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Moon is Earth's companion in space.

questions.question: Which type of rock is granite?
questions.correctAnswer: Igneous
questions.explanation: Granite forms when magma cools slowly underground, so it is igneous.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Granite is a cooled magma rock.

questions.question: How long does it take Earth to revolve around the Sun?
questions.correctAnswer: About 365 days
questions.explanation: Earth travels all the way around the Sun once a year; that trip is what we call a year.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: One trip around the Sun equals one year.

questions.question: What is an earthquake?
questions.correctAnswer: A sudden shaking of the ground caused by movement in Earth's crust
questions.explanation: Earthquakes happen when built-up stress in rocks is released suddenly along a fault.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Earthquakes are the ground shaking from slipping rock.

questions.question: What is a full moon?
questions.correctAnswer: The phase when the Moon's whole lit side faces Earth
distractors: The phase when the Moon is invisible
The phase when the Moon is half lit
A moon that is extra large
questions.explanation: At full moon, Earth is between the Sun and the Moon, so we see the fully lit side.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A full moon shows its whole bright face.

questions.question: What is an aquifer?
questions.correctAnswer: An underground layer of rock that holds water
questions.explanation: Aquifers are rock layers that store groundwater people can pump out.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Aquifers are underground water storage.

questions.question: What is erosion?
questions.correctAnswer: The movement of weathered material by water, wind, or ice
distractors: The breaking of rock in place
The growth of plants on rock
questions.explanation: A river can carry sand for miles and drop it far away - that moving, not the breaking, is erosion.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Erosion moves what weathering broke.

questions.question: What is an asteroid?
questions.correctAnswer: A rocky object orbiting the Sun, smaller than a planet
distractors: A ball of ice with a tail
questions.explanation: Asteroids are rocky bodies, mostly found in the belt between Mars and Jupiter.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Asteroids are space rocks.

questions.question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercury
questions.explanation: Mercury orbits closest to the Sun, so it has the shortest year of any planet - just 88 Earth days.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mercury is the Sun's nearest neighbor.

questions.question: What is a new moon?
questions.correctAnswer: The phase when the Moon's dark side faces Earth
distractors: The phase when the Moon is full
The phase when the Moon is half lit
questions.explanation: At new moon, the side of the Moon facing Earth is not lit by the Sun.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A new moon is all dark from our view.

questions.question: Which type of rock forms from cooled lava or magma?
questions.correctAnswer: Igneous rock
questions.explanation: Lava cooling on the surface makes fine-grained rock like basalt, while magma cooling slowly underground makes coarse-grained rock like granite.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Igneous means born from fire.

questions.question: What is the rock cycle?
questions.correctAnswer: The process by which rocks change from one type to another over time
questions.explanation: Through melting, cooling, weathering, and heat and pressure, rocks transform into other types.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Rocks recycle through melting, cooling, and pressure.

questions.question: What galaxy do we live in?
questions.correctAnswer: The Milky Way
questions.explanation: On a dark night you can see the Milky Way as a pale band of light - that is our galaxy seen from the inside.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: We live in the Milky Way.

questions.question: What is deposition?
questions.correctAnswer: The dropping off of eroded material in a new place
questions.explanation: Deposition happens when wind, water, or ice slows down and drops the material it carried.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Deposition is nature setting material down.

questions.question: What is mechanical weathering?
questions.correctAnswer: Physical breaking of rock without changing its chemistry
questions.explanation: Mechanical weathering includes freezing water, plant roots, and temperature changes cracking rock.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mechanical weathering is breaking without chemistry.

questions.question: What is a watershed?
questions.correctAnswer: An area of land where water drains into a common river or lake
questions.explanation: Every drop of rain that falls in a watershed flows downhill into the same river - your school and home may share one.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A watershed is a drainage neighborhood.

questions.question: Which planet is known as the Morning Star or Evening Star?
questions.correctAnswer: Venus
questions.explanation: Venus is bright in the sky near sunrise or sunset.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Venus shines brightest at dawn and dusk.

questions.question: What is lava?
questions.correctAnswer: Molten rock on Earth's surface
questions.explanation: Lava is magma that has reached Earth's surface.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Lava is magma out in the open.

questions.question: Which planet is farthest from the Sun?
questions.correctAnswer: Neptune
questions.explanation: Neptune is the eighth and farthest planet from the Sun.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Neptune is the last stop from the Sun.

questions.question: What instrument measures temperature?
questions.correctAnswer: A thermometer
questions.explanation: A thermometer works because liquids like alcohol expand as they warm, rising up the tube.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Thermometers measure temperature.

questions.question: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.correctAnswer: Jupiter
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet, more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Jupiter is the giant of the solar system.

questions.question: Which type of rock forms when heat and pressure change an existing rock?
questions.correctAnswer: Metamorphic rock
questions.explanation: Metamorphic rocks form when heat and pressure transform a rock without melting it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Metamorphic means changed form.

questions.question: Which type of rock forms from layers of sediment pressed together?
questions.correctAnswer: Sedimentary rock
questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks form when sediments are compacted and cemented over time.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sedimentary rocks are built from layers.

questions.question: What is the Ring of Fire?
questions.correctAnswer: A zone around the Pacific Ocean with many volcanoes and earthquakes
distractors: A ring of fire around the Sun
questions.explanation: The Ring of Fire follows plate boundaries around the Pacific, where many volcanoes and quakes occur.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Ring of Fire circles the Pacific with volcanoes.

questions.question: Why does the Moon appear to change shape?
questions.correctAnswer: We see different amounts of its sunlit side
distractors: Earth's shadow covers it each night
questions.explanation: Moon phases happen because we see different portions of the Moon's lit half as it orbits Earth.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Moon phases are a trick of sunlight and angle.

questions.question: What is a comet?
questions.correctAnswer: An icy body that grows a glowing tail near the Sun
questions.explanation: Comets are made of ice and dust; heat from the Sun makes them release gas and form a tail.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Comets are icy snowballs with glowing tails.

questions.question: What is humidity?
questions.correctAnswer: The amount of water vapor in the air
questions.explanation: On a humid day the air is already full of water vapor, so your sweat cannot evaporate - that is why it feels sticky.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Humid air feels sticky because it holds water vapor.

questions.question: What is the ozone layer?
questions.correctAnswer: A layer in the stratosphere that absorbs harmful UV radiation
questions.explanation: Without the ozone layer, far more ultraviolet rays would reach the ground and damage skin and crops.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ozone is Earth's sunscreen layer.

questions.question: What is the main cause of ocean tides?
questions.correctAnswer: The Moon's gravity
questions.explanation: The Moon's gravity pulls ocean water toward it, creating bulges that we see as tides.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Moon's pull makes the tides.

questions.question: What happens at a convergent plate boundary?
questions.correctAnswer: Plates move toward each other
questions.explanation: At convergent boundaries plates collide, which can form mountains or cause one plate to sink.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Convergent means coming together.

questions.question: What is condensation?
questions.correctAnswer: Water vapor cooling and changing into liquid
questions.explanation: Condensation is when water vapor cools and forms tiny liquid droplets, like on a cold glass.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Condensation is vapor turning back into droplets.

questions.question: What is chemical weathering?
questions.correctAnswer: Rock breaking down by chemical changes
questions.explanation: Chemical weathering changes the minerals in rock, such as acid rain dissolving limestone.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Chemical weathering changes what the rock is made of.

questions.question: Which gas is the main greenhouse gas from burning fossil fuels?
questions.correctAnswer: Carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Burning coal, oil, and gas releases carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Burning fuels adds carbon dioxide to the air.

questions.question: What is infiltration?
questions.correctAnswer: Water soaking into the ground
questions.explanation: Rain soaks through soil and cracks in rock until it reaches groundwater - paved streets block infiltration, so water runs off instead.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Infiltration is water sinking into the ground.

questions.question: How long does it take Earth to rotate once?
questions.correctAnswer: About 24 hours
questions.explanation: Earth spins like a top, turning once every 24 hours - one full spin is one day.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: One spin equals one day.

questions.question: What is a star?
questions.correctAnswer: A ball of hot gas that makes its own light through fusion
questions.explanation: Stars shine because nuclear fusion in their cores releases huge energy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Stars make their own light by fusion.

questions.question: What is a fault?
questions.correctAnswer: A crack in Earth's crust where rocks move
questions.explanation: A fault is a fracture where blocks of rock slide past each other.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Faults are the cracks where earthquakes start.

questions.question: Which layer of Earth is liquid metal?
questions.correctAnswer: The outer core
questions.explanation: The outer core is made of liquid iron and nickel.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The liquid outer core flows around the solid inner core.

questions.question: Which type of rock is marble?
questions.correctAnswer: Metamorphic
questions.explanation: Marble forms when limestone is changed by heat and pressure.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Marble is limestone transformed by heat and pressure.

questions.question: What is a tornado?
questions.correctAnswer: A violently rotating column of air reaching the ground
questions.explanation: Tornadoes form in severe thunderstorms and spin fast in a narrow path.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A tornado is a spinning funnel from a storm cloud.

questions.question: What is the asteroid belt?
questions.correctAnswer: A region between Mars and Jupiter with many asteroids
questions.explanation: The asteroid belt lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The asteroid belt sits between Mars and Jupiter.

questions.question: What force pulls objects toward Earth?
questions.correctAnswer: Gravity
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls the Moon toward Earth too, which is why the Moon stays in orbit instead of flying away.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Gravity keeps your feet on the ground.

questions.question: What is transpiration?
questions.correctAnswer: Water vapor released from plants into the air
questions.explanation: Plants release water vapor through tiny openings in their leaves.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Plants breathe out water vapor.

questions.question: What causes the seasons?
questions.correctAnswer: The tilt of Earth's axis
distractors: Earth getting closer to the Sun
questions.explanation: Earth's tilted axis makes sunlight hit each hemisphere more directly at different times of year.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The tilt, not the distance, makes the seasons.

questions.question: What is the biosphere?
questions.correctAnswer: All living things on Earth
questions.explanation: The biosphere stretches from deep ocean vents to the tops of mountains - wherever living things can survive.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The biosphere is Earth's living zone.

questions.question: What causes day and night on Earth?
questions.correctAnswer: Earth rotating on its axis
questions.explanation: As Earth spins, different parts face the Sun (day) or face away (night).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Earth's spin makes the Sun seem to rise and set.

questions.question: What is evaporation?
questions.correctAnswer: Liquid water changing into water vapor
questions.explanation: Evaporation happens when liquid water gains energy and becomes a gas.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Evaporation is water rising into the air as vapor.

questions.question: What is a hurricane?
questions.correctAnswer: A large rotating tropical storm with strong winds
questions.explanation: Hurricanes form over warm ocean water and have a calm eye at the center.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Hurricanes are giant spinning ocean storms.

questions.question: What is a delta?
questions.correctAnswer: Land formed where a river deposits sediment at its mouth
questions.explanation: Deltas form when a river slows at the sea and drops its sediment.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Deltas are river-built land at the sea.

questions.question: What is a solar eclipse?
questions.correctAnswer: The Moon blocking the Sun's light
distractors: The Sun going behind a cloud
questions.explanation: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes between Earth and the Sun.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The Moon's shadow causes a solar eclipse.

questions.question: What is precipitation?
questions.correctAnswer: Water falling from the atmosphere to Earth
questions.explanation: Precipitation is rain, snow, sleet, or hail falling from clouds to the ground.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Precipitation is water falling from the sky.

questions.question: What is the summer solstice?
questions.correctAnswer: The longest day of the year in a hemisphere
distractors: The shortest day of the year
The day with equal day and night
questions.explanation: In the Northern Hemisphere the summer solstice falls around June 21, when the North Pole tilts most toward the Sun.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The summer solstice is the longest day.

questions.question: What is a lunar eclipse?
questions.correctAnswer: Earth blocking sunlight from reaching the Moon
questions.explanation: A lunar eclipse happens when Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Earth's shadow causes a lunar eclipse.

questions.question: What is a glacier?
questions.correctAnswer: A large mass of ice that moves slowly over land
distractors: A frozen lake that never moves
questions.explanation: Glaciers are huge rivers of ice that flow and carve the land.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Glaciers are slow-moving rivers of ice.

questions.question: What instrument measures wind speed?
questions.correctAnswer: An anemometer
questions.explanation: An anemometer has spinning cups that measure how fast the wind blows.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: An anemometer's cups spin faster in stronger wind.

questions.question: What is the Coriolis effect?
questions.correctAnswer: The curving of wind and ocean currents caused by Earth's rotation
questions.explanation: Earth's rotation makes moving air and water curve, to the right in the Northern Hemisphere.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Earth's spin curves the wind.

questions.question: Why does the Moon not crash into Earth?
questions.correctAnswer: Its forward motion balances Earth's gravity
distractors: There is no gravity in space
It is too light to fall
questions.explanation: The Moon is constantly falling toward Earth but moving forward fast enough to keep missing it, which is an orbit.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Orbiting is falling and missing forever.

questions.question: What is magma?
questions.correctAnswer: Molten rock below Earth's surface
questions.explanation: Magma is molten rock beneath the surface; once it erupts, it is called lava.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Magma is lava that is still underground.

questions.question: What happens at a divergent plate boundary?
questions.correctAnswer: Plates move away from each other
questions.explanation: At divergent boundaries plates separate, and new crust forms, often at mid-ocean ridges.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Divergent means moving apart.
